items.text: COMMITTEE DISCHARGED AND COMMITTED TO RULES

items.actClause:
AN ACT to amend the transportation law, in relation to requiring the
commissioner of transportation to establish methods of reporting safety issues
with limousines
items.memo:
BILL NUMBER: S6185

SPONSOR: MAY
 
TITLE OF BILL:  An act to amend the transportation law, in relation to
requiring the commissioner of transportation to establish methods of
reporting safety issues with limousines

 
PURPOSE OR GENERAL IDEA OF BILL:

This legislation requires the State Department of Transportation (DOT)
to establish a hotline, website, and smartphone application to report
safety and customer service issues with stretch limousines.

 
SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS:

Section one of the bill requires DOT to establish a smartphone applica-
tion, website and toll-free hotline for purposes of reporting customer
service or safety issues with a stretch limousine. DOT would be required
to consider such reports for purposes of withdrawing a motor carrier's
operating authority or denying new authority applications, and would be
required to affix signage in for-hire limousines providing information
for these resources. Finally, DOT is required to design a scoring system
for customer service reports, and is also required to design a reporting
system for substantiated claims of safety issues by customer or individ-
uals with knowledge of such issues or compliance failures.

Section two provides the effective date.

 
JUSTIFICATION:

One of the tragedies of the Schoharie limousine crash from October 6,
2018 came from reporting that many of the vehicle's passengers were
communicating numerous potential safety issues with their friends and
family members who were outside of the vehicle. Unfortunately, there was
not a simple way for these reports of potential vehicle defects to be
communicated to the governmental bodies with regulatory authority over
the vehicles so that it would be aware.

Further, during the Senate's first hearing on limousine safety, a number
of limousine owners and operators discussed their concerns with bad
actors who fail or refuse to comply with DOT laws and inspection
requirements, and their inability to report instances where they knew
vehicles were operating unlawfully. These witnesses also discussed the
need for improved communication between agency regulators.

This legislation seeks to address this information gap by allowing
customers and other observers to contact the DOT if there are substanti-
ated issues with a stretch limousine.

 
PRIOR LEGISLATIVE HISTORY:

New Bill

 
FISCAL IMPLICATIONS:

To be determined.

 
EFFECTIVE DATE:
180 days after being signed into law.

A.memo:
BILL NUMBER: S6185A

SPONSOR: MAY
 
TITLE OF BILL:

An act to amend the transportation law, in relation to requiring the
commissioner of transportation to establish methods of reporting safety
issues with stretch limousines

 
PURPOSE OR GENERAL IDEA OF BILL:

This legislation requires the State Department of Transportation (DOT)
to establish a hotline, website, and smartphone application to report
safety issues with respect to stretch limousines and their drivers.

 
SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS:

Section one of the bill requires DOT to establish a smartphone applica-
tion, website and toll-free hotline for purposes of reporting safety
issues with respect to stretch limousines and their operators.  DOT
would be required to coordinate with the Department of Motor Vehicles
(DMV) in establishing and maintaining the application, website and
hotline. DOT and DMV may investigate reports generated through these
media, and would be authorized to consider such reports for enforcement
purposes and for policymaking.  DOT is also directed to report on the
reports received from these platforms and discuss how it used the infor-
mation.

Section two provides the effective date.

 
JUSTIFICATION:

One of the tragedies of the Schoharie limousine crash from October 6,
2018 came from reporting that many of the vehicle's passengers were
communicating numerous potential safety issues with their friends and
family members who were outside of the vehicle. Unfortunately, there was
not a simple way for these reports of potential vehicle defects to be
communicated to the governmental bodies with regulatory authority over
the vehicles so that it would be aware.

Further, during the Senate's first hearing on limousine safety, a number
of limousine owners and operators discussed their concerns with bad
actors who fail or refuse to comply with DOT laws and inspection
requirements, and their inability to report instances where they knew
vehicles were operating unlawfully. These witnesses also discussed the
need for improved communication between agency regulators.

This legislation seeks to address this information gap by allowing
customers and other observers to contact the DOT if there are substanti-
ated issues with a stretch limousine.

 
PRIOR LEGISLATIVE HISTORY:

New Bill (S.6185) passed the Senate without objection in 2019.

 
FISCAL IMPLICATIONS:

To be determined.

 
EFFECTIVE DATE:
One year after being signed into law.

B.memo:
BILL NUMBER: S6185B

SPONSOR: MAY
 
TITLE OF BILL:

An act to amend the transportation law, in relation to requiring the
commissioner of transportation to establish methods of reporting safety
issues with stretch limousines

 
PURPOSE OR GENERAL IDEA OF BILL:

This legislation requires the State Department of Transportation (DOT)
and Department of Motor Vehicles (DMV) to establish a hotline and
website to report safety issues with respect to stretch limousines and
their drivers.

 
SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS:

Section one of the bill requires DOT and DMV to establish and/or main-
tain a website and toll-free hotline for purposes of reporting safety
issues with respect to stretch limousines and their operators.  DOT
would be required to coordinate with the Department of Motor Vehicles
(DMV) in establishing and maintaining the website and hotline. DOT and
DMV may investigate reports generated through these media, and would be
authorized to consider such reports for enforcement purposes and for
policymaking.  DOT is also directed to report on the reports received
from these platforms and discuss how it used the information.  Building
off of the 2019 Adopted Budget reforms with respect to posting of
inspection status and driver qualifications, the bill language requires
the website and hotline to be conspicuously posted within stretch limou-
sines for all passengers to be able to view them.

Section two provides the effective date.

 
JUSTIFICATION:

One of the tragedies of the Schoharie limousine crash from October 6,
2018 came from reporting that many of the vehicle's passengers were
communicating numerous potential safety issues with their friends and
family members who were outside of the vehicle. Unfortunately, there was
not a simple way for these reports of potential vehicle defects to be
communicated to the governmental bodies with regulatory authority over
the vehicles so that it would be aware.

Further, during the Senate's first hearing on limousine safety, a number
of limousine owners and operators discussed their concerns with bad
actors who fail or refuse to comply with DOT laws and inspection
requirements, and their inability to report instances where they knew
vehicles were operating unlawfully. These witnesses also discussed the
need for improved communication between agency regulators.

This legislation seeks to address this information gap by allowing
customers and other observers to contact the DOT if there are substanti-
ated issues with a stretch limousine.

 
PRIOR LEGISLATIVE HISTORY:

New Bill (S.6185) passed the Senate without objection in 2019.

 
FISCAL IMPLICATIONS:

It is expected that the website and hotline can be provided within
existing agency resources.

 
EFFECTIVE DATE:
One year after being signed into law.

summary: Requires the commissioner of transportation to establish, maintain, monitor and publicize a hotline operated and maintained by the department of motor vehicles through which any person may report safety issues with stretch limousines and to use such reports when determining withdrawing a motor carrier's operating authority or denying applications for new or revised operating authority.
title: Relates to requiring the commissioner of transportation to establish methods of reporting safety issues with stretch limousines
